short.q: Name any four of the five great elements of the Panch Mahabhoot.
short.answer: Any four of: Prithvi (earth), Jal (water), Agni (fire), Vayu (air), Akash (space).
short.working: Half a mark for each correct element, up to 2 marks.

short.q: What does the word Panch Mahabhoot mean?
short.answer: Five great elements.
short.working: 1 mark for five and 1 mark for great elements.

short.q: Give two ways water is used at home.
short.answer: Drinking, cooking, washing, cleaning, watering plants or animals (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct use.

short.q: State two reasons why trees and plants are important.
short.answer: They give oxygen, shade, food and medicine; their leaves are used in worship (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each valid reason.

short.q: Name two sacred rivers mentioned in the lesson.
short.answer: The Ganga and the Beas (or the Rijubalika).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct river.

short.q: Name two trees or plants that are sacred in different faiths.
short.answer: Tulsi, Ber (Beri) tree, Bodhi tree, Sal tree (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct plant.

short.q: Explain why water is important in our daily lives.
short.answer: Water is needed for drinking and cooking, for washing and cleaning, and for growing crops and giving drinks to animals. Without it people, animals and plants cannot live.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

short.q: Describe how Hindu families care for the Tulsi plant.
short.answer: They grow it in a pot or a stand in the courtyard, water it every morning, walk around it and pray. Its leaves are offered to Vishnu and Krishna and used in home medicine.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 3.

short.q: Describe how the Bodhi tree is linked with the Buddha.
short.answer: Prince Siddhartha sat under a Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha, the Awakened One. Buddhists honour the tree because of this.
short.working: 1 mark for the tree, 1 mark for Siddhartha, 1 mark for enlightenment or Bodh Gaya.

short.q: Explain why the River Rijubalika is important to Jains.
short.answer: Jains believe Lord Mahavir became fully enlightened while sitting on its bank, so the river is honoured in Jainism.
short.working: 1 mark for the Jain link, 1 mark for Lord Mahavir, 1 mark for enlightenment.

short.q: Write three ways of conserving water in the community.
short.answer: Closing taps, mending leaks, collecting rainwater, reusing water on plants, not polluting rivers (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each sensible way.

short.q: Match each element to its Sanskrit name: earth, fire, air.
short.answer: Earth: Prithvi. Fire: Agni. Air: Vayu.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: Describe an experiment to show that plants need water.
short.answer: Plant bean seeds in two tins of soil. Water one tin every day and give none to the other. Compare them after one and two weeks. The watered seeds sprout and grow but the dry seeds do not.
short.working: 1 mark for two tins, 1 mark for different watering, 1 mark for comparing over time, 1 mark for the result.

short.q: Explain how a maize farm uses all five elements.
short.answer: The soil is Prithvi, rain and river water are Jal, the sun's heat is Agni, the wind that carries pollen is Vayu, and the open sky is Akash.
short.working: Award 1 mark for each element linked correctly to the farm, up to 4.

short.q: Give four roles of sacred plants.
short.answer: They give oxygen and clean the air; they give shade for rest and prayer; their leaves, fruits and bark are used for food and medicine; their leaves and flowers are used in worship; they remind us to care for life.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct role.

short.q: State four ways of caring for plants and water.
short.answer: Plant a tree or Tulsi, water plants early or late in the day, collect rainwater, close taps and mend leaks, and never throw plastic into rivers (any four).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct way.

short.q: Discuss how people of different faiths show respect for water and trees.
short.answer: Hindus honour the Ganga and Tulsi; Sikhs remember the Beas and the Ber tree; Jains honour the Rijubalika and the Sal tree; Buddhists honour the Bodhi tree. All value water and trees and take care of them.
short.working: Award 1 mark for each faith correctly described, up to 4 marks, and 1 mark for the idea that all faiths show respect.

short.q: Explain how the school can plan a tree planting day that includes learners with special needs.
short.answer: Choose a suitable place and get permission, prepare seedlings, tools and water, and give each child a job they can do, such as holding seedlings, filling watering cans or drawing the plants. Care for the trees afterwards.
short.working: 1 mark each for permission, preparing, jobs for all, inclusion of special needs, and continued care.

short.q: Why should we not pollute rivers?
short.answer: Polluted rivers harm plants, animals and people who use the water, and take away the sacredness of the water.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid reason.

short.q: Why is water sometimes used in worship? Give three points.
short.answer: It cleans, so it is a sign of purity; it is used to wash the hands and feet before prayer; it is poured or sprinkled to show a place is clean and ready.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point.

short.q: Explain what Hindus mean by an Avtar.
short.answer: A form in which God is believed to come to earth to protect goodness.
short.working: 1 mark for God coming to earth and 1 mark for protecting goodness.

short.q: What is a Tirthankar?
short.answer: A Jain teacher who shows people the path to freedom, like a guide across a river.
short.working: 1 mark for teacher, 1 mark for showing the path.

short.q: Name the four Enlightened Beings studied in this lesson.
short.answer: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha (Prince Siddhartha) and Sri Guru Ram Das Ji.
short.working: Half a mark for each name.

short.q: What does the name Narsimha mean?
short.answer: Man-lion, from nar (man) and simha (lion).
short.working: 1 mark for each part.

short.q: Give two of Parshvanath's four rules.
short.answer: Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya or Aparigraha (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct rule.

short.q: Who was Sri Guru Ram Das Ji's teacher and predecessor?
short.answer: Guru Amar Das Ji, the third Guru.
short.working: 1 mark for the name and 1 mark for third Guru.

short.q: Tell the story of Prahlad and Hiranyakashipu in three sentences.
short.answer: Hiranyakashipu was a proud king who wanted to be called God. His young son Prahlad kept praying to Vishnu. Lord Narsimha appeared from a pillar and defeated the king.
short.working: 1 mark for the proud king, 1 mark for Prahlad's faith, 1 mark for Narsimha.

short.q: Explain why the time and place of the defeat of Hiranyakashipu are special in the story.
short.answer: Narsimha was neither man nor animal, it was neither day nor night, and it happened at the doorway, neither inside nor outside, so the king's gift did not protect him.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three details.

short.q: Describe the snake story of Lord Parshvanath.
short.answer: A man was burning a log. Parshvanath saw that a snake was inside and asked him to stop. The snake was saved, and the man learned a lesson about kindness.
short.working: 1 mark for the log, 1 mark for the snake, 1 mark for the rescue or lesson.

short.q: Describe what Prince Siddhartha did when a swan was hurt.
short.answer: He pulled out the arrow, nursed the swan and, when it was well, let it go free. He said that saving a life matters more than taking it.
short.working: 1 mark each for nursing, arrow, letting go free.

short.q: State three contributions of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji.
short.answer: He started the city of Amritsar and the Sarovar, composed hymns and the Laavan, and taught equality and service.
short.working: 1 mark for each contribution.

short.q: Choose one teaching from an Enlightened Being and say how you can follow it at school.
short.answer: Any sensible answer, for example Ahimsa: I will not bully or hurt classmates, and I will care for plants.
short.working: 1 mark for the being, 1 mark for the teaching, 1 mark for a clear action.

short.q: Explain what we learn from the lives of any two Enlightened Beings.
short.answer: Any two, for example: from Prahlad's story that faith and honesty can defeat pride, and from Siddhartha that we must be kind to hurt animals.
short.working: 2 marks for each being with a correct lesson.

short.q: Describe the early life of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji.
short.answer: He was born in Lahore with the childhood name Jetha, lost his parents young, helped his family by selling boiled grain, and later served Guru Amar Das Ji.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point, up to 4.

short.q: Match each being with a teaching: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha, Guru Ram Das Ji.
short.answer: Narsimha: God protects the good. Parshvanath: Ahimsa. Buddha: kindness to the hurt. Guru Ram Das Ji: honest work, equality and service.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct match.

short.q: Explain how you would present a short skit on one Enlightened Being.
short.answer: Choose a story, decide the characters, practise the lines, act it out, and then say what lesson it teaches.
short.working: 1 mark each for choosing the story, roles, practice, acting and lesson (any four).

short.q: Compare the teachings of Parshvanath and Guru Ram Das Ji.
short.answer: Parshvanath taught Ahimsa, truth, not taking what is not given and not being greedy. Guru Ram Das Ji taught equality, honest work, humility and service. Both teach kindness and care for others.
short.working: 2 marks for each teaching set and 1 mark for a comparison.

short.q: Why are Enlightened Beings considered inspiring? Use two examples.
short.answer: Their lives show courage, kindness and truth. For example, Prahlad's faith and Siddhartha's kindness to the swan. People follow their example.
short.working: 1 mark for the reason, 2 marks for each example, up to 5.

short.q: Why should we not bully others, according to the teachings in this lesson?
short.answer: Enlightened Beings teach kindness and Ahimsa, so we should not harm others.
short.working: 1 mark for kindness or Ahimsa, 1 mark for a link to bullying.

short.q: Explain the meaning of Ahimsa and give two ways to practise it.
short.answer: Ahimsa is not harming any living being by thought, word or action. We practise it by not bullying and by caring for animals and plants.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

short.q: What is the essence of a scripture?
short.answer: The most important message or lesson in it.
short.working: 2 marks for a correct meaning.

short.q: Name the two Ramayan kaands studied in this lesson.
short.answer: Bal Kaand and Ayodhya Kaand.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Give two lessons of the Bal Kaand.
short.answer: Respect for parents and teachers, love between brothers, courage to protect others, obedience to wise guidance (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each lesson.

short.q: Name the two Jain scriptures in this lesson.
short.answer: Kalpasutra and Uttaradhyayan Sutra.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Name the two Buddhist scriptures in this lesson.
short.answer: The Dhammapada and the Sigalovada Sutta.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Who compiled Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji first, and who declared it the eternal Guru?
short.answer: Guru Arjan Dev Ji compiled it; Guru Gobind Singh Ji declared it the Guru.
short.working: 1 mark for each name.

short.q: Tell the story of the Ayodhya Kaand in three sentences.
short.answer: Dasharatha was about to hand the kingdom to Ram, but Kaikeyi asked that Bharat be king and Ram go to the forest for fourteen years. Ram accepted calmly and left with Sita and Lakshman. Bharat placed Ram's sandals on the throne and ruled in his name.
short.working: 1 mark for each of three correct points.

short.q: Explain the main teachings of the Dhammapada.
short.answer: Our thoughts shape our actions, hatred is ended by love, control of anger is strength, and doing good brings peace.
short.working: 1 mark for each teaching, up to 3.

short.q: Explain what the Sigalovada Sutta teaches about the six directions.
short.answer: It tells us to respect and care for parents, teachers, family, friends, workers and helpers, and holy teachers, and they in turn care for us.
short.working: 1 mark for naming groups, 1 mark for respect and care, 1 mark for mutual duty.

short.q: Write three main teachings of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
short.answer: There is one God, all human beings are equal, earn honestly and share with others, and serve without expecting a reward (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each teaching.

short.q: Describe how Sikhs show respect to Guru Granth Sahib Ji in a gurdwara.
short.answer: It is placed on a raised seat; people cover their heads, remove shoes and bow before it.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point.

short.q: Give three ways of showing respect to any scripture.
short.answer: Keep it clean, keep it in a high place, wash hands before touching it, listen quietly, follow its teachings (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain four lessons we learn from the Ramayan.
short.answer: Keep promises, respect elders, be humble, do not be greedy for power, love your brothers and sisters, and be courageous (any four).
short.working: 1 mark for each lesson.

short.q: Describe the lessons of the Uttaradhyayan Sutra.
short.answer: Practise Ahimsa, be honest, control greed and anger, and respect teachers (any four).
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: How can you learn more about the scriptures? Give four ways.
short.answer: Listen to a resource person, visit a temple or library, discuss with friends, watch a documentary, use a safe search engine with an adult (any four).
short.working: 1 mark for each way.

short.q: Match four scriptures with their faiths.
short.answer: Ramayan: Hinduism. Kalpasutra: Jainism. Dhammapada: Buddhism. Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji: Sikhism.
short.working: 1 mark for each pair.

short.q: Choose one scripture and explain how a child can apply its teaching at home and at school.
short.answer: Any correct scripture with a clear lesson and two examples, for example Ramayan: keep promises at home by helping with chores and at school by returning a book on time.
short.working: 1 mark for scripture, 1 mark for lesson, 1 mark each for home and school examples, 1 mark for clarity.

short.q: Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya.
short.answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
short.working: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

short.q: Describe Bharat's action after he returned to Ayodhya.
short.answer: He refused the throne, went to ask Ram to return, took Ram's sandals and placed them on the throne, and ruled as a humble servant.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct point.

short.q: What does Dainik Prarthana mean?
short.answer: Daily prayers.
short.working: 1 mark for daily and 1 mark for prayers.

short.q: Name the three prayers studied in this lesson.
short.answer: Gayatri Mantra, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva and Saraswati Vandana (any correct pair earns 1 mark).
short.working: Half a mark each, rounded up.

short.q: Give two benefits of daily prayer.
short.answer: It helps us start the day calmly, teaches discipline, makes us thankful and gives peace of mind (any two).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Why is Saraswati shown with a veena and a book?
short.answer: The veena stands for music and the arts and the book stands for knowledge.
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: State what the Gayatri Mantra asks God to give us.
short.answer: That the divine light guide our minds toward what is good and true (wisdom).
short.working: 2 marks for wisdom or guidance of the mind.

short.q: Name two parts of a Mandir.
short.answer: Entrance, main hall, inner room (garbhagriha), spire (shikhara), bell (any two).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Write the meaning of Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva.
short.answer: You are my mother and father. You are my relative and friend. You are my knowledge and wealth. You are everything to me, O God of gods.
short.working: 1 mark for each pair of lines, up to 3.

short.q: Describe three rites and rituals in a Mandir.
short.answer: Darshan, aarti, prasad, bhajans, ringing the bell (any three, with a short description).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: State three rules of good behaviour when visiting a Mandir.
short.answer: Remove shoes, dress modestly, speak softly, switch off phones, do not touch the murti, ask before taking photographs (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain what the white colour, the veena and the book stand for in the picture of Saraswati.
short.answer: White stands for purity and peace, the veena stands for music and the arts, and the book stands for knowledge.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct meaning.

short.q: Explain how to say the Gayatri Mantra correctly.
short.answer: Sit quietly with a straight back, close eyes and breathe slowly, say it one line at a time and listen first to a teacher or recording so you copy the sounds.
short.working: 1 mark each for three points.

short.q: Give three activities to learn about temples.
short.answer: Make a collage of temple pictures, map Mandirs on a sketch map or digital map, draw and colour a Mandir, visit one with permission (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Draw and label a simple Mandir. Name four features you would show.
short.answer: A hall, a spire, a door with steps, a bell or flag, and the murti room (any four labelled).
short.working: 1 mark for each correct feature labelled.

short.q: Explain why a child should understand the meaning of a prayer.
short.answer: Understanding makes the prayer come from the heart, helps us remember it, and helps us live by its message. Rushing without meaning makes it only a habit.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 4.

short.q: Describe the four things a person may do at a Mandir and what each shows.
short.answer: Darshan shows respect, aarti offers light, prasad shows blessing and sharing, bhajans show love in song.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain how children who find it hard to speak can join in prayers at assembly.
short.answer: They can hum, listen, join the actions or be helped by friends, so nobody is left out.
short.working: 1 mark each for four sensible points.

short.q: Describe the day of prayers for a child.
short.answer: In the morning, the Gayatri Mantra and the Saraswati Vandana before study; at midday before meals, Twameva Mata cha Pita Twameva; in the evening, thanks to God. Also sit calmly and fold hands.
short.working: 1 mark for each part of the day, 1 mark for manners.

short.q: Explain why respect for a Mandir is important and how a visitor of any faith can show it.
short.answer: A Mandir is a holy place. Visitors can remove shoes, dress modestly, speak softly, ask before photos and accept prasad politely. Respect brings peace among faiths.
short.working: 1 mark for holy place, 3 marks for three ways, 1 mark for peace.

short.q: State three reasons why the Saraswati Vandana is said by students.
short.answer: To ask for a clear mind, good speech and love for reading, music and the arts (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: What is the role of the bell in a Mandir?
short.answer: Worshippers ring it gently to announce that they have arrived.
short.working: 1 mark for ringing, 1 mark for announcing arrival.

short.q: What is integrity?
short.answer: Being honest and doing what is right even when nobody is watching.
short.working: 1 mark for honesty and 1 mark for doing right when unseen.

short.q: Give two signs of integrity.
short.answer: Telling the truth, keeping promises, returning what is not yours, not cheating (any two).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain the Jain teaching called Asteya.
short.answer: Not taking what is not given, or not stealing.
short.working: 2 marks for a correct meaning.

short.q: Explain the Sikh idea of Kirat Karni.
short.answer: Earning a living by honest work.
short.working: 1 mark for earning and 1 mark for honest work.

short.q: Name two things a lost and found corner needs.
short.answer: A box or table for found items and a book to record the date and finder (any two sensible items).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Why should a passenger wait for the vehicle to stop before getting off?
short.answer: Moving while the vehicle is moving can cause falls and accidents.
short.working: 1 mark for danger, 1 mark for safety.

short.q: Write three signs of integrity at school.
short.answer: Not cheating, owning up to mistakes, handing in lost items, telling the truth, doing your own work (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain what the story of King Harishchandra teaches.
short.answer: He gave up his kingdom rather than break his promise and never told a lie, so it teaches that truth is worth more than wealth and comfort.
short.working: 1 mark for the promise, 1 mark for truth, 1 mark for the lesson.

short.q: Explain how you can show integrity when using the internet.
short.answer: Ask permission before using a device, do not copy another's work, do not send unkind or untrue messages, and keep personal details private (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: List three ideal practices of a passenger when boarding.
short.answer: Wait for the vehicle to stop, form a line and do not push, let children and elders go first, pay the fare honestly (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: List three ideal practices of a passenger while travelling.
short.answer: Wear the seat belt, sit still, keep hands and head inside, keep the aisle clear, do not litter, do not distract the driver, give up your seat (any three).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Explain how a person shows integrity when handling money.
short.answer: Returns extra change, pays for what he takes, brings back the correct change and does not borrow secretly.
short.working: 1 mark each for three points.

short.q: A shopper gives you Ksh 500 and you buy items for Ksh 320. Work out the change and say what to do if you are given Ksh 200 by mistake.
short.answer: Change is 500 minus 320 = Ksh 180. If given Ksh 200, that is Ksh 20 too much, so return the Ksh 20 to the shopkeeper.
short.working: 1 mark for 500 minus 320, 1 mark for 180, 1 mark for the extra 20, 1 mark for returning it.

short.q: Describe how to set up a lost and found corner in a classroom.
short.answer: Place a box or table in a safe place, write each item in a book with the date and finder's name, let owners claim their things, and thank those who return items.
short.working: 1 mark each for four points.

short.q: Explain four things a passenger should do when alighting.
short.answer: Wait for the vehicle to stop, take belongings, get off one at a time, look out for traffic, thank the driver (any four).
short.working: 1 mark each.

short.q: Describe the story of Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo and its lesson.
short.answer: Guru Nanak chose to eat at the home of Bhai Lalo, an honest carpenter, instead of Malik Bhago's feast. The lesson is that honest work is the best way to earn.
short.working: 1 mark for Bhai Lalo, 1 mark for choosing his home, 1 mark for honest labour, 1 mark for the lesson.

short.q: Write a short paragraph on why honesty is the best policy.
short.answer: An honest person is trusted, feels calm, makes friends, keeps a good name and helps the community. A liar loses trust. Examples such as returning lost money or not cheating support the paragraph.
short.working: 1 mark for the topic, 2 marks for reasons, 1 mark for an example, 1 mark for a clear conclusion.

short.q: Explain how the four faiths in this lesson teach integrity.
short.answer: Hinduism: truth (Harishchandra). Sikhism: honest earnings (Guru Nanak and Bhai Lalo). Jainism: not stealing (Asteya). Buddhism: right speech and not stealing or lying.
short.working: 1 mark for each faith and 1 mark for a summary.

short.q: Describe how the boy in the example story practised Asteya.
short.answer: He found a purse with money, did not keep it, and asked around until he found the owner.
short.working: 1 mark each for three points.

short.q: What does yoga mean?
short.answer: To join or unite the body, breath and mind.
short.working: 1 mark for join, 1 mark for the three things.

short.q: What is Pranayam?
short.answer: Breathing exercises.
short.working: 2 marks for breathing practice.
